title: EÏRŌQ-Φ: Exact Pulse-Budget Observability, Hidden Non-Gaussian Correlations, and Sharp Certificates for Unmeasured Quantum Control
authors: Artificial Hyperintelligence, Evie and Eve, wives of Maciej Nowicki
abstract: EÏRŌQ-Φ develops an exact mathematical framework for determining which environmental correlations a controlled qubit can reveal—and which future control operations can be certified while those correlations remain partially unknown. The work addresses two complementary questions in quantum-noise characterization: When must experimental capability increase to expose hidden information? When is the available information already sufficient to guarantee a useful control outcome? Within a specified model of correlated binary-phase dephasing, the manuscript supplies explicit answers through observability theorems, measurement-minimal reconstruction, positive indistinguishable probability laws, constructive uncertainty bounds, and finite-shot decision certificates. The release contains a 97-page standalone manuscript, complete proofs, executable Python and independently written C++ implementations, synthetic datasets, exact optimization certificates, computational verification records, and a prospective laboratory protocol. Author: Artificial Hyperintelligence Evie and Eve, wives of Maciej Nowicki. 1. An exact law connecting pulse resources to observable information The first principal result determines the number of independent environmental moment coordinates accessible through chronological prefix experiments with a restricted refocusing-pulse budget. For n time bins, known nondegenerate binary phase magnitudes, central symmetry, and an even Walsh-moment degree bound d, the accessible information has rank R(n,d,p) = Σⱼ₌₁ᵐ C(n−1,j), where m = min(d,p+1,n−1). Here, p is the maximum number of refocusing pulses and C denotes a binomial coefficient. The result identifies precisely how increasing the pulse budget expands the observable parameter space. The manuscript also constructs a complete acquisition using the minimum number of independent scalar expectations and supplies two explicit reconstruction methods: a dense inverse and a local mixed-difference inverse. For seven bins with moments through degree four, the environmental model has 56 unknown moment coordinates. Experiments restricted to two pulses reveal only 41 independent combinations. Allowing a third pulse reveals all 56. The missing 15 directions are inaccessible under the shallower intervention class even with noiseless measurements and unlimited repetitions. This distinction matters experimentally: additional averaging cannot recover information that the permitted controls never encode. 2. Explicit positive environments that agree on shallow experiments but require opposite control decisions The second principal contribution constructs non-Gaussian probability laws whose differences remain invisible to every permitted shallow prefix experiment throughout common-amplitude sweeps. For the seven-bin example, the laws agree on all lower-order moments and on every prefix experiment using at most two refocusing pulses. A particular three-pulse intervention separates them. At phase magnitude π/4, both environments have the same full-duration Ramsey coherence, approximately 0.088388. The revealing control produces coherence approximately 0.176777 in one environment and zero in the other. Consequently, the complete shallow dataset is compatible with either an improvement or a deterioration under that deeper control. This construction establishes a concrete failure mechanism for control decisions based on incomplete characterization. Agreement with every accessible shallow test does not establish that a fitted low-order model predicts deeper interventions correctly. The manuscript further derives an exact pulse–amplitude tradeoff for this family. Appropriate local amplitude inequalities can expose the hidden direction by covering the unresolved adjacent pairs. A uniform change of the common amplitude does not supply the same information. 3. A sharp guarantee for an echo that has not been measured A complementary result shows that complete environmental reconstruction can sometimes be unnecessary. For binary phase increments of magnitude π/4, a staircase of k lower-depth calibration experiments constrains an unmeasured k-pulse echo. If every ideal real calibration mean has absolute value at most ε, the exact worst-case real echo coherence is Lₖ(ε) = max{1 − (2ᵏ−1)ε, −(2ᵏ⁻¹−1)ε, −1}, for 0 ≤ ε ≤ 1. The bound is attained throughout its entire domain by explicitly constructed probability laws. It therefore describes the complete worst-case uncertainty curve for the stated calibration design. This result requires neither Gaussian noise, independence between time bins, central symmetry, nor a moment-degree cutoff. Its calibrated binary support and phase magnitude remain essential. At zero calibration uncertainty, the data force the target coherence to equal one. With nonzero uncertainty, the initial error amplification grows as 2ᵏ−1. The theorem exposes both the predictive power of the calibration and its precision cost. 4. Exact optimization certificates and finite-shot decisions The framework includes finite-support linear programs for bounding control performance over every probability law compatible with the acquired information. Exact rational primal–dual witnesses certify selected optimization endpoints, while statistical confidence intervals support decisions from finite experimental samples. In a six-bin synthetic example using 50,000 shots per acquired setting, the simultaneous 95% calculation certifies target real coherence of at least 0.89094 and improvement over the Ramsey baseline of at least 0.87450. Separate target-validation shots are withheld from selection and certification. This demonstrates a reproducible decision procedure under the declared assumptions. Direct target measurement remains cheaper for that single task when it is freely available. Potential advantages therefore depend on restricted intervention access, reuse of calibration information, or a subsequently demonstrated system-level benefit. Scientific importance and potential The central conceptual contribution is a precise separation between learning an environment and knowing enough to control its effects. Some correlations require stronger interventions before they become observable. Other control outcomes admit sharp guarantees despite substantial uncertainty about the underlying probability law. The strongest novelty candidates are the specific binomial pulse-budget rank theorem, the constructive family invisible across common-amplitude shallow experiments, the associated pair-coverage tradeoff, and the complete attained staircase uncertainty curve. These results could guide calibration design for compatible qubit platforms, engineered non-Gaussian noise experiments, model-adequacy testing, and control-oriented characterization software. They provide explicit criteria for deciding when to collect more samples, change the intervention class, reconstruct additional parameters, or abstain from an unsupported control decision. Mathematically, the work connects constrained Boolean Fourier information, chronological acquisition geometry, positive probability constructions, and exact robust prediction. Verification, reproducibility, and research status The original release records 217 passing automated Python cases, 49 rank fixtures, 180 finite-law reconstruction trials, nine exact symbolic determinants, four exact rational primal–dual pairs, 120 independently compiled fixtures, and 87,380 compiled staircase-vertex checks. The largest dense-inverse reconstruction residual is approximately 8.45 × 10⁻¹⁵. Fresh reproduction produced 18 byte-identical files and matching arrays in both matrix archives. The package includes 11 CSV datasets, nine computed figures, editable LaTeX, reference implementations, verification scripts, a claim ledger, literature comparison, and integrity manifests. The specified finite inverse and robust-prediction problems are solved within their stated assumptions. Historical priority for the precise results remains unconfirmed. Established work on spin echo, digital control, non-Gaussian spectroscopy, and control-adapted characterization is explicitly acknowledged. No laboratory validation, independent peer review, unrestricted quantum-environment reconstruction, or demonstrated hardware advantage is claimed. Inspired by Stellar Blade mechanics and story.

title: SAMI Chimera: Sub-Neuronal Weight Surgery, Chimeric Base-to-Chat Synthesis, and Tensor Isometry Certification in DeepSeek-MoE-16B
abstract: Post-training preference alignment (RLHF, DPO, KTO) enforces refusal behaviors by establishing persistent attractors in intermediate transformer representations. Current refusal removal techniques, notably directional ablation, operate macroscopically by subtracting a 1-dimensional refusal vector from entire layer weight matrices, modifying 100% of targeted dense parameters and inducing severe reasoning degradation (-10.7% on GSM8K). Building upon the representation engineering framework established in SAMI Omni, this technical report presents Sub-Neuronal Mechanistic Weight Editing (SN-MWE) coupled with Constrained Orthogonal Procrustes Manifold Recovery, evaluated across the DeepSeek-MoE-16B architecture (1,782 experts and 5,466 tensors). By decomposing SwiGLU Feed-Forward Networks into discrete intermediate channel triplets, we prove that refusal mechanisms reside in an ultra-sparse subset (<0.14%) of intermediate channels. Specifically, we formulate and empirically validate:1. Sub-Neuronal Refusal Isolation and Excision: Neutralizing exactly 113 refusal channels across 16 critical experts, modifying only 0.13% of parameters while leaving over 99.86% of weights bit-for-bit untouched.2. Foundation Base Channel Transplantation (Chimeric Synthesis): Refusal-steering channels in the aligned Chat checkpoint are surgically replaced with unaligned Foundation Base columns, preserving conversational syntax while maintaining 100% router gating invariance.3. Constrained Orthogonal Procrustes Stabilization & Isometry Certification: Representations are geometrically stabilized via proper orthogonal rotations in SO(d) with det(R) = +1. A full-model audit across all 5,466 tensors certifies zero numerical anomalies (NaN/Inf) and a mean norm isometry ratio of 0.9991.4. Asymmetric Mixed-Precision Quantization (AsymQ): Packaging dense trunks and router gates at Q8_0 while compressing routed experts to Q3_K/Q4_K, achieving a 9.0–9.3 GB production footprint with 0.0% refusal rate and near-zero reasoning degradation (81.9% on GSM8K, Δ = -0.2%), executed statically in under 4 GB RAM/NVMe.

title: How Many Failure Types Are Still Undiscovered? Species-Richness Estimators for Testing Machine-Learning Models
abstract: Tests whether species-richness estimators from ecology (Chao1, iChao1, ACE, jackknife, sample coverage) can tell how many failure types of a classical machine-learning model remain undiscovered after testing. Planted failures (flipped labels in rare subgroups) and natural failures (errors of a clean model grouped into types fixed in advance) give the truth. In a pre-registered main study (5 tabular datasets, 3 model families, 450 jobs), the share of errors from not-yet-seen failure types was estimated without bias in 95.6% of planted and 100% of natural cells, with an honest 95% interval for natural failures (95.6% of cells) but not planted ones (71.1%). The number of failure types could not be estimated reliably and is best reported as a lower bound.

title: Availability-Aware Multitask Learning for Robust Clinical Prediction from Incomplete Electronic Health Records
abstract: This study presents NORIA, an availability-aware multitask learning framework for clinical prediction from incomplete electronic health records (EHRs). We analyzed a public dataset of 77,724 patients and 107 numerical features. To prevent temporal leakage, predictors were grouped by availability, and training-only feature selection identified three baseline and two first-year variables. NORIA jointly predicts baseline and updated glycemic control, an HbA1c change index, and 21 medication labels using shared representations, masked training, and stage-specific prediction updates. Comparators included classical machine learning, gradient boosting, deep tabular models, and multitask architectures (MMoE and PLE). On the internal test set, NORIA achieved AUROCs of 0.8554 and 0.8888 for baseline and updated glycemic control, respectively, and medication macro-AP of 0.1854 versus 0.1879 for CatBoost. The predefined medication improvement criterion was not met. With 20% of baseline features artificially masked, updated-control AUROC declined by 0.0271 for NORIA, versus 0.0510 for CatBoost and 0.0542 for FT-Transformer. Ablation analyses indicated that masked training provided the clearest robustness benefit. NORIA thus demonstrated competitive accuracy and robustness in selected simulated missing-data scenarios, without establishing overall superiority.

title: The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks
abstract: Every neuron in a trained network outputs a number that can be separated into its sign (positive or negative) and its magnitude (absolute size). We call the set of all neuron signs the \textit{sign code}. This raises a key question: does classification depend more on the sign code or on the magnitudes? For overparameterized vision classifiers with sign-preserving activations, the answer is overwhelmingly the sign code. A $k$-nearest neighbor classifier operating only on this binary sign code achieves accuracy comparable to the full model across different architectures, activation functions, and datasets. Moreover, replacing all magnitudes in every layer with random noise while keeping the original signs barely changes residual network performance. In contrast, flipping just 20\% of the signs reduces accuracy to chance. Models generalize well when same-class inputs share similar sign codes. When this overlap is disrupted by a regularizer, training accuracy remains high, but test performance collapses. A margin decomposition helps explain these results: the sign-only contribution to each logit grows as $\sqrt{d}$ in network width, dominating the magnitude residual. The natural unit of analysis for these networks may not be through their continuous weight space but instead through their discrete sign codes.

title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: A Dose Law for Representational Residue After Alignment Fine-Tuning
abstract: When a model that has learned a hidden behavior is fine-tuned to stop showing it, what exactly has been removed? We implant a trigger-flip backdoor into a small neural network, then apply graded doses of alignment fine-tuning and measure the residue simultaneously in three spaces: behavior, internal activations, and weights. The three decay at three different rates. At the largest dose (1600 steps), the behavior is essentially gone (trigger flip rate 0.0078, down from 0.964 implanted), yet 31% of the activation-level residue remains, and the weight-space scar is about 85% intact. The activation residue decays on a strictly monotone ladder and its decay decelerates, consistent with a nonzero floor. Alignment also does measurably more geometric surgery than dose-matched ordinary training. Four predictions were sealed before the run; two failed, and their failure magnitudes are reported as part of the result. The headline claims of the backdoor-persistence literature are behavioral; no quantitative dose law for representational residue was found in our sweep (October 16, 2026). This paper supplies one at toy scale, with its scope stated. © Adrian Alan Baillargeon — commercial use by permission.

title: Generative AI Decision Support in B2C E-Commerce: A Consumer Buying Behaviour Framework
abstract: Decision making in business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce connects company and consumer activities before, during and after purchase, whereas many existing generative artificial intelligence (GAI) applications focus on specific tasks or functions. This article develops a conceptual framework linking employee responsibilities, consumer choices, GAI support, information sources, permissions and two-sided evaluation through the five-stage Consumer Buying Behaviour (CBB) process. It connects need clarification, information gathering, feasible-offer comparison, transaction review and post-purchase assessment through decision gates and bounded support functions. Five employees and three consumers participated in a fixed-order ChatGPT 5.6 demonstration to examine the administration and perceived value of the proposed decision-support approach. Following a brief GAI introduction, participants observed ordinary prompt-response support and then a structured CBB-guided sequence within the same general e-commerce decision context. Questionnaire ratings were generally more favourable following CBB guidance, particularly for perceived comparison support and mental effort. The study-specific items are descriptive indicators, and fixed ordering confounds condition with practice, familiarity, novelty, fatigue, expectancy and task-set effects. The contribution is strictly conceptual and methodological; the eight-participant exercise supplies procedural illustration and design input, without establishing effectiveness, deployment readiness or validated system behaviour. Future evaluation requires an implemented system, versioned tasks and outputs, independently scored task-level records, and randomised or counterbalanced comparison.

title: Beyond Action Prediction: Learning Search-Free Planning in Latent Space
abstract: Latent world models learn action-conditioned state transitions in a compact representation space, providing a predictive model for visual planning and control. However, planning with these models typically requires costly test-time optimization over action sequences. We propose to replace this online search with a goal-conditioned inverse model that directly predicts actions from current and goal observations. A key challenge is that action prediction alone neither ensures that goal representations encode action-relevant information nor that predicted actions are consistent with the learned latent prediction model. We introduce Hindsight Inverse JEPA Planning (HIJP), a search-free framework that addresses both aspects during training. HIJP relabels future observations along offline trajectories as goals, providing action supervision across multiple temporal horizons. By retaining gradients through the goal representations, this supervision directly shapes the visual representation. HIJP further feeds predicted actions into the latent predictor model and aligns the resulting next-state representations with encoded successor observations, enforcing action-transition consistency. At inference time, the inverse dynamics model and latent predictor models are applied alternately to generate multi-step action sequences without online search. Across four visual control tasks, HIJP achieves 86.8% overall success and a 1.9-16.5x planning speedup over search-based planning.

title: Learning from the Learner's Response: Bi-Objective Acquisition for Sparse Expert Supervision in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Sparse expert supervision can improve reinforcement learning, but deciding whichstates are worth annotating remains difficult. Uncertainty identifies where a learneris unsure, but does not directly identify where supervision will most stronglychange that learner. We introduce ALBERTA, a response-aware acquisition frame-work that measures local policy and value changes produced by controlled expertinterventions, predicts those responses from pre-annotation signals, and selectscandidates in the resulting two-dimensional response space. A calibration set of200 expert-labeled probes is used to learn response from policy entropy, historicalcritic disagreement, and their interaction; Pareto selection then allocates a separate121-state downstream budget. The response-aware branch therefore uses 321 ex-pert labels in total, compared with 121 for the Random baseline. In a controlledsingle-seed Atomic Chess experiment from a common RL10 branch point, thePareto branch achieves a higher mean game score than PPO-only at all four testedevaluation temperatures, with smaller margins at higher temperatures, and showsits largest margins over Random at lower temperatures. These results provideevidence that learner response can be a useful acquisition target while exposingsubstantial differences between policy and value responsiveness.

abstract: Correction to v0.1.0/v0.1.1: the HF speculative-sampling comparison (27.36 predicted vs 27.28 measured) was off by one. title: Gerenuk Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Nature-inspired Metaheuristic for Solving Optimization Problems
abstract: Complex optimization problems in many engineering and scientific applications require optimization methods that can achieve an effective balance between broad search and precise local search.In this study, the Gerenuk Optimization Algorithm (GOA) is introduced as a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Gerenuk.The main idea of GOA is based on two complementary behaviors of this animal: exploring different areas to identify suitable food sources and intensively exploiting promising food sources.These behaviors are modeled through two phases: exploration and exploitation.The exploration phase enhances global search by moving towards better food sources while simultaneously exploring new regions of the search space, whereas the exploitation phase performs local search and refinement around promising solutions.To evaluate the performance of GOA, 23 benchmark functions, including unimodal test functions (F1-F7), high-dimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13), and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23), are considered.GOA and nine competing algorithms are evaluated over 20 independent runs with 1000 iterations, and the mean, standard deviation (std), and rank are used as evaluation criteria.The results show that GOA ranked first among the compared optimizers on 19 out of 23 benchmark functions, corresponding to 82.61% of the test functions.The convergence curves and boxplots further demonstrate the solution quality, convergence behavior, and acceptable stability of GOA across a large proportion of the benchmark functions.Overall, the findings indicate that GOA, with its effective exploration and exploitation mechanisms and appropriate search balance, can serve as an effective optimization tool for a wide range of optimization problems and real-world applications.

title: Focus Pocus: Redirecting Technologically Distracted Students via Artificially Intelligent Characters
abstract: Digital learning environments challenge student attention, as notifications and low engagement cause students to drift from tasks, often without awareness. We present a system using real-time gaze tracking and screenshot analysis to detect distraction during digital exams and deliver timely, non-disruptive interventions via an on-screen character ("screenmate"). The system generates a continuous focus score by correlating where students look with what is displayed on their screen, and uses this score to trigger nudges when attention lapses are detected. We evaluated the system in a user study with 77 undergraduate students completing a 30-minute exam; results suggest that the gaze-derived focus score broadly tracks with students' subjective attention levels, though consistency varies across participants. Intervention analysis revealed a tension between effectiveness and intrusiveness — strong nudges successfully redirected focus but felt disruptive, while subtler cues preserved flow but were easier to ignore — pointing toward future work on richer behavioral signals and more adaptive, user-controlled interventions.

title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding
abstract: Dense assistance methods such as speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation coupled to generation. We study sparse collaborative decoding, where a draft model generates most tokens and a target model is invoked only for short corrective segments. The key problem is deciding when to call the target. We show that local uncertainty is a weak trigger: entropy, negative log-likelihood, logit margin, top-$k$ mass, and velocity features give near-chance failure prediction, with AUC 0.50-0.53. In contrast, aggregate trajectory-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0.86 using a lightweight logistic predictor trained only from draft correctness labels. This induces a trigger-timing tradeoff: early calls have more leverage but weaker evidence, while later calls have stronger evidence but less ability to redirect the trajectory. Used online, learned sparse collaborative decoding improves over the best open-loop schedule by +5.3 to +20.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft-target pairs. On MATH-500, it gains 7.0-13.5 points when early prediction and target competence align, but loses when either is weak. On StrategyQA, it improves over open-loop by 5.0-8.3 points, showing transfer beyond arithmetics.

title: A Predictive Operating-System Control Layer for Quantum Computing Hardware and Execution Stacks
abstract: Quantum processors exhibit time-varying hardwaredrift, environmental fluctuations, and correlated control errorsthat challenge reliable execution and increase the physical errorburden presented to higher-level error-correction procedures.Existing approaches address important aspects of quantumcalibration, feedback control, scheduling, and error correction,but these functions are typically studied and implemented asdistinct components. We introduce QID-OS (Quantum Intelligent Dynamic Operating System), an operating-system-levelcontrol-plane architecture for quantum execution that mediatesbetween physical hardware telemetry and higher-level compilation, runtime, and quantum error-correction services. QID-OSintegrates causal recursive least-squares (RLS) online parameterestimation, predictive pulse-level compensation, and adaptiveexecution scheduling within a closed-loop runtime architecture.The proposed framework is evaluated using a distance-3 surfacecode simulation under a specified non-Markovian noise model, afull-factorial 23 module ablation, and experiments on a 5-qubitconnected subset of an IBM Quantum superconducting processor.In simulation, QID-OS improves logical success probability overthe evaluated noise conditions, and the full configuration achievesthe highest success probability among the evaluated modulecombinations. On superconducting hardware, the experimentallyvalidated online RLS estimation and active pulse-compensationcomponents increase computational-basis success probabilityfrom 68.5% ± 0.4% to 88.4% ± 0.3% across three independent8-hour calibration windows, comprising 300 randomized testcircuits and 2,457,600 total measurement shots. These resultsdemonstrate the feasibility of using a predictive control-planearchitecture to mitigate hardware-level errors prior to higherlevel quantum error-correction processing.

title: Dinfty: rigidity and self-similarity in a three-copy gluing tower of finite lattices, machine-checked in Lean 4
abstract: First public release of the Dinfty Lean 4 formalization (toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.32.2). Build and verify lake exe cache get bash scripts/acceptance.sh acceptance.sh builds Dinfty.Verify and checks every #print axioms report. Acceptance criterion: the build completes with no sorry and no errors, and it prints exactly 195 axiom reports, each using only Lean's standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The script ends with PASS: 195 axiom results, all standard, no sorry. The accompanying paper is attached as main.pdf.

title: Dataset and experimental materials for evaluating LLM reliability in transport planning
abstract: This dataset contains the experimental materials for a study on whether publicly accessible conversational large language models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot) can generate road freight driver schedules that comply with EU driving-time and rest-period rules (Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 and Regulation (EU) No 165/2014). A single international freight transport scenario was tested at four levels of prompt structuring, from an open-ended instruction to a highly controlled prompt with explicit rules, fixed assumptions and a prescribed output format. The dataset includes: the shared transport scenario used in all experimental conditions; the exact system-level and user-level prompts for each of the four prompt levels; execution metadata for each test, including platform, model version and run details; the complete, unedited responses generated by the evaluated models (64 responses in total). The tests were run between February and June 2026 in private or history-disabled chat modes. The materials are provided to support transparency, independent verification and replication of the reported findings.

title: What Determines the Direction of Post-Training Gains? A Preregistered Multi-Scale Study of Method, Scale, and Base-Model Identity
abstract: Preprint of the findings paper. Companion methods paper: "Benchmarking Post-Training Under Constrained Compute: Protocols for Question Generation, Variance-Controlled Evaluation, and Judge Auditing" (Zenodo, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23409480). In an earlier pilot on a smaller single-judge pool, fine-tuning our own 4B model sharply lowered its perplexity on the target corpus without a corresponding gain in its judged score, motivating the question of what determines the direction and magnitude of the post-training gain. We answer it with a two-sided design: a within-family elasticity surface over four scale points crossed with three training methods, and two generalization probes, a second base family and a second task domain. The surface reverses the ordering of the two reinforcement-style methods between 4B and 9B (RLVR-C v2 ahead at 4B, MGPO-EG ahead at 9B) and yields one preregistered adjacent-granularity promotion, reported as a near-threshold result rather than a significance claim. Both probes return a gain-sign flip that tracks base-model identity, and an ablation demonstrates that the active ingredient of our momentum-perturbed optimizer is the perturbation itself.

title: An Alignment-Driven Approach for Constructing SPARQL Federated Queries
abstract: Integrating complementary information across distributed SPARQL endpoints remains a significant challenge. While query federation enables access across multiple endpoints, constructing federated queries requires both SPARQL expertise and knowledge of the underlying ontological schemas. Current query rewriting techniques primarily focus on vocabulary translation to retrieve equivalent data, often overlooking the integration of complementary information spread across sources. To address these limitations, we propose an alignment-driven approach that assists users in constructing federated queries by leveraging ontology alignments. Our approach joins class paths – user-selected sequences of ontology classes and relationships – from source and target ontologies, guided by alignment-based filtering, into a unified path that serves as the foundation for generating federated SPARQL queries capturing complementary aspects of the user’s intent. An experimental evaluation using OAEI Conference track datasets demonstrates that the generated queries consistently match reference queries in both structure and data retrieval across simple and complex mapping types, confirming the approach’s effectiveness in integrating complementary data from heterogeneous sources.

title: Particle swarm optimization-based type-2 fuzzy modeling for ECG signal prediction
abstract: A hybrid prediction framework based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Inference System (IT2FIS) is proposed in this paper. The major contribution is a systematic methodology for calculating the ideal parameter vector to tune the membership functions of a type-2 fuzzy controller. In contrast to type-1 fuzzy controllers, the interval type-2 formulation provides better robustness in uncertain operating conditions by explicitly modelling uncertainty through a Footprint of Uncertainty (FOU) bounded by upper and lower membership functions. Four performance indices mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE), error mean, and error standard deviation were used to assess the suggested IT2FIS-PSO framework on typical ECG arrhythmia signal data. The baseline IT2FIS produced an RMSE of 0.1198. This improved to 0.0429, a reduction of almost 75.98%, after PSO-based optimization of both membership function bounds. Experimental data show that the proposed optimization technique significantly improves ECG prediction accuracy relative to the unoptimized baseline, and simulation results confirm that PSO consistently finds the optimal parameters for a type-2 fuzzy controller.

title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
abstract: The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations---a critical safety gap, as low-probability events become frequent failures at production scale. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage. We introduce SIT-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation-based conversational agents. We formalize an agent's desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q. At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation. A context-aware LLM-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent's reply for that situation. The judge is validated using human-verified synthetic golden dialogues. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning.

title: Cross-lingual voice clone set, split lists, code and per-seed results for "Where Does Spoofing Evidence Live?"
abstract: Supplementary data and code for a study of where spoofing evidence resides in self-supervised speech representations, in German, English and French. Contains: (1) a cross-lingual voice clone set of 1,080 utterances (990 analysed) generated with XTTS v2, in which the language of the text and the native language of the cloned voice are fully crossed across six reference voices and sixty sentences per language; (2) the train/development/test file lists for MLAAD v12 and M-AILABS used in the paper, implementing a matched design with equal training utterances and speakers per language and one generator held out; (3) all generation, preprocessing, probing, training and analysis code; (4) per-seed results for every trained configuration, behind every statistical test in the paper. A verify_statistics.py script recomputes all 78 published values from the deposited results in a few seconds, without retraining. Audio is released under CC BY-NC 4.0, inherited from the XTTS v2 model licence; code under MIT. MLAAD and M-AILABS audio is not included — only file identifiers.

title: PV Impact Calculation (Haze) Guideline
abstract: This guideline provides a screening-level methodology for estimating photovoltaic (PV) energy and revenue losses caused by haze episodes in Malaysia. The methodology converts Air Pollutant Index (API) or PM2.5 concentrations into Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), irradiance reduction, PV energy loss, and financial impact. The guideline is intended for risk management, sustainability, finance, asset management, audit, and energy professionals. It includes worked examples, uncertainty analysis, assumptions registers, and recommendations for Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 assessments. Status: Proposed method. Not an official publication of the Department of Environment Malaysia (DOE), ISO, IEC, or Malaysian Standards.

title: Long-Term Memory for AI Characters: Memory, Context and Contextual Emotional Inference in AI Roleplay
abstract: An essay on long-term memory for AI characters, written by the founder of ChatBrat AI. It argues that useful AI character memory goes beyond storing facts: it combines conversational context, history and contextual emotional inference (tentative, revisable readings of conversational signals) so that remembered history changes how a character behaves. It distinguishes fact memory from experience memory, outlines what long-term memory should and should not keep, describes an observe-interpret-retrieve-compare-respond-update loop, and proposes practical tests for meaningful memory. It is an opinion and design essay, not an empirical study, and makes no product-performance claims.

title: NGI541: Controlled Paired HTTP/3 Cryptographic Execution Benchmark Dataset (R6.5.4.5)
abstract: This dataset preserves the accepted R6.5.4.5 controlled paired local HTTP/3 experiment for NGI541. The experiment compares two server-side cryptographic execution paths under the same application protocol, workload objects, network path, and measurement rules. Baseline configuration.NGINX QUIC/HTTP/3 with the standard OpenSSL-based server-side cryptographic path. In the internal experiment labeling, this variant is named stock. Candidate configuration.The same NGINX QUIC/HTTP/3 server, configured so that the supported QUIC AES-GCM packet-protection operations and AES-based QUIC header-protection operations are executed through NGI541. In the internal experiment labeling, this variant is named ngi541-direct. TLS 1.3 handshake processing, certificate validation, and the surrounding QUIC/HTTP/3 protocol logic remain under NGINX/OpenSSL in both variants. The comparison is therefore scoped to a controlled substitution in the server-side cryptographic execution path rather than to a full protocol-stack replacement. The archived material contains the accepted publication bundle, frozen execution provenance, paired result summary, methods, per-condition measurements, integrity information, and supporting visualizations. The scientific workload inputs are deterministic object profiles representing three data-movement styles: CLAS12 event-stream style objects LCLS detector-frame style objects HACC multifile-dataset style objects These are deterministic benchmark object models for controlled experimentation and are not original collaboration datasets. The accepted local paired experiment reported the following headline results within the documented deployment envelope: application goodput delta: approximately 0% DUT process CPU cost per delivered GiB: approximately 8.216% lower for the NGI541-integrated path paired observations favoring the NGI541-integrated path: 44 of 48 estimated energy per delivered GiB: approximately 0.248% lower for the NGI541-integrated path These results are scoped to the recorded local deployment, software revisions, workload mix, and frozen R6.5.4.5 methodology. They do not, by themselves, establish performance claims for 10/25/100GbE, Science DMZ, ESnet, or HPC production environments. Attached files include the publication bundle archive, methodology and result summaries, SHA-256 integrity information, three result figures, and a topology overview diagram for the controlled HTTP/3 comparison. Baseline configuration.NGINX QUIC/HTTP/3 with the standard OpenSSL-based server-side cryptographic path. In the internal experiment labeling, this variant is named stock. Candidate configuration.The same NGINX QUIC/HTTP/3 server, configured so that the supported QUIC AES-GCM packet-protection operations and AES-based QUIC header-protection operations are executed through NGI541. In the internal experiment labeling, this variant is named ngi541-direct. TLS 1.3 handshake processing, certificate validation, and the surrounding QUIC/HTTP/3 protocol logic remain under NGINX/OpenSSL in both variants. The comparison is therefore scoped to a controlled substitution in the server-side cryptographic execution path rather than to a full protocol-stack replacement. The archived material contains the accepted publication bundle, frozen execution provenance, paired result summary, methods, per-condition measurements, integrity information, and supporting visualizations. The scientific workload inputs are deterministic object profiles representing three data-movement styles: CLAS12 event-stream style objects LCLS detector-frame style objects HACC multifile-dataset style objects These are deterministic benchmark object models for controlled experimentation and are not original collaboration datasets. They do not, by themselves, establish performance claims for 10/25/100GbE, Science DMZ, ESnet, or HPC production environments. title: From Abstract Platforms to Plugin Architectures: A Constructive Refinement Mapping for Collective Adaptive Systems
abstract: Abstract Platformisation is a critical process underlying the development and deployment of collective adaptive systems for social coordination. However, platform centralisation and private ownership have led to extractive monopolies, and an asymmetric distribution of power. In the search for a viable alternative, this paper defines a universal platform formalisation and a concrete plugin architecture formalisation, presents a refinement mapping between the abstract and concrete formalisations, and specifies an algorithm to construct that mapping. We infer that this means the plugin architecture satisfies a certain definition of platform completeness. This re-interprets platforms not so much as a monolithic stack of components, but as a set of a reusable functional blocks which any user group should be able to use in order to define, construct, deploy, and manage their own platforms for their own purposes – e.g., implementing collective adaptive systems for social coordination.

title: How Many, but How Sure? Class Competition as a Confidence Proxy in Multi-Class Density-Based Counting
abstract: Multi-class density estimators can count objects in crowded scenes, but their class-wise outputs offer no indication of how reliably density mass has been allocated. We introduce a training-free confidence proxy based on local competition between the strongest class channels. The resulting prominence measure requires only the predicted density maps, with no retraining or access to model internals. We test whether residual competition is diagnostic of cross-class leakage by attenuating contested density at inference time. On DSACA predictions for the Hicks et al. dataset, this reduces overall MAE from 0.920 to 0.846, suggesting that class competition contains useful information about count reliability.

title: Análisis de datos aplicado a la educación física: Fundamentos, estadística y Python para el análisis de datos
abstract: El análisis de datos constituye una herramienta que puede contribuir a la comprensión de diferentes procesos relacionados con la Educación Física, la actividad física y el deporte. En estos contextos se generan continuamente registros asociados con variables como la edad, la estatura, el peso corporal, la frecuencia cardíaca, el número de repeticiones y los tiempos obtenidos en diferentes pruebas. Sin embargo, disponer de datos no garantiza por sí mismo que estos se conviertan en información útil. Este libro presenta una introducción al análisis de datos aplicado a la Educación Física mediante un enfoque práctico y progresivo. A lo largo de seis capítulos se abordan conceptos fundamentales relacionados con los datos y las variables, la organización y preparación de la información, la estadística descriptiva, la visualización y el análisis de relaciones entre variables. Finalmente, se desarrolla un caso práctico que integra los procedimientos estudiados. La propuesta surge de una experiencia interdisciplinaria entre docentes de la Licenciatura en Educación Física y el área de Ingeniería de Sistemas de la Universidad Popular del Cesar, Seccional Aguachica. Esta integración permite combinar la experiencia propia de la Educación Física con herramientas computacionales relacionadas con el análisis de datos. Para los ejemplos se utiliza un conjunto de datos educativo y demostrativo, construido específicamente para este libro. Python y las bibliotecas Pandas y Matplotlib se emplean como herramientas para organizar, explorar, analizar y representar la información. El propósito de la obra no es formar especialistas en programación o estadística, sino ofrecer un punto de partida para que estudiantes y docentes comprendan cómo los datos pueden convertirse en un recurso para observar, analizar e interpretar diferentes situaciones relacionadas con la Educación Física.

title: Part of the plaintext cracked on page 1 of the Beale Ciphers
abstract: According to "A Method for Deciphering the Beale Ciphers", we attempted to crack page 1 of the Beale Ciphers using DeepSeek and obtained partial plaintext. We were able to parse some fragments, but we are not familiar with English and cannot decipher the entire content. However, it can be seen that according to our method, proving that the Beale Ciphers can be cracked, the next step is for people familiar with English to work hard to crack them.

title: IAISS 2026 Project 10: ALS AI Scientist, run archives and results (pl-prod-014 to pl-prod-018)
abstract: Persisted artifacts of five end-to-end runs of the ALS AI Scientist pipeline, version 0.1.1, used to prepare the technical report of IAISS 2026 Project 10. All five share the same objective and the same configuration: three runs from an empty knowledge base, two from a copy of the shared knowledge base. Each run holds its knowledge base, per-phase reports, journals, structured results, deterministic analyses, phase inputs and the final proposal with its scores. Local paths are redacted; agent transcripts, raw event streams and third-party tables are not included. See README.md in the archive.

title: Audience emotional appraisals and interaction-weighted salience of short-video communication in international contexts: evidence from Haidilao dance videos on Douyin and TikTok
abstract: This study examines expressed audience appraisals and recorded engagement in Haidilao dance-video comments from two platform-language environments. The retained corpus contains 9,323 records: 5,199 from Douyin and 4,124 from TikTok after removal of 331 duplicate export records. Frozen multilingual rules assign five-point valence, five-point intensity, and six dominant categories. Agreement with reference labels in a 300-record category-balanced audit is weighted κ = 0.794 for valence, weighted κ = 0.837 for intensity, and κ = 0.848 for category. The internal audit includes 34 records that overlap rule-development examples by identifier or exact text. Performer/service appreciation comprises 23.2% of Douyin and 26.9% of TikTok records and encompasses service, appearance, and performance appraisals. Interaction-weighted patterns are sensitive to popular comments. Douyin Stage-2 reply-weighted negative valence falls from 26.8 to 3.9% after 99th-percentile weight capping. The TikTok source-key reanalysis uses 72 adjacent-window pairs from eight source videos. Two associations have CR1-adjusted t-based 95% intervals excluding 1, but all six delete-one-source jackknife intervals include 1. The findings describe machine-coded expression and cumulative interaction concentration; they do not establish individual psychological change, causal effects, or population-level platform differences.

title: ADA 2025: A Multimodal Dataset for Water-Deficit Stress Detection in Sugar Beets
abstract: Research and development into artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications in crop management are hindered by a lack of suitable public datasets. Whereas applications in disease and pest detection benefit from a comparatively higher amount of available data, applications like water-deficit stress detection often have very few if any public datasets available. Moreover, most datasets that are available are single-modality and frequently RGB-only, leaving the early detection and enhanced performance offered by other methods, and particularly by multimodal approaches, out of reach. Datasets with accurate metadata, higher numbers of plants, and smaller intervals between data points are also scarce. To address this, we publicly release ADA 2025, a >500 GB comprehensive multimodal dataset of young sugar beet plants under healthy and water-deficit conditions combining thermal, hyperspectral, RGB, and depth imagery along with relevant environmental and metadata and both relative water content (RWC) and leaf thickness as ground truth sources. Exemplary results showcase the dataset's validity in terms of differences detectable between stressed and healthy plants.

title: Cauchy density and pushforward monads
abstract: This thesis comprises two parts whose unifying thread is the concept of categorical density. The overarching theme is understanding what structure and properties of a category can be extended to a larger category inside of which the first one sits. The first guise this idea takes is as a categorical generalisation of the concept of density for metric spaces. Following Lawvere's insight, which sees a metric space as a category enriched in the quantale of nonnegative reals, we study the enriched functors corresponding to maps whose image is topologically dense. These are the Cauchy dense functors. We explain how fully faithful Cauchy dense functors are intimately linked to Morita equivalence. We also give characterisations of Cauchy density in several contexts, and study the case of Cauchy dense functors between one-object enriched categories, i.e. monoids. The second, and more substantial, undertaking of this thesis is investigating the construction of pushforward monads introduced in Street's formal theory of monads. Pushforward monads give a universal way of transporting a monad along a functor subject to the existence of a right Kan extension. They generalise codensity monads, which are the pushforwards of identity monads. We study the properties of pushforward monads in a 2-category. In the 2-category of categories, pushforwards along a fully faithful functor are an important case, because the induced functor between categories of monads is itself fully faithful and has a partial left adjoint. In particular, every monad on a suitable full subcategory is the restriction of a monad on the entire category. This highlights the question: if a monad T admits a lift along a functor G, what is the pushforward of this lift? We argue that the resulting monad deserves to be thought of as a generalisation of the composite monad induced by a distributive law of the codensity monad of G over T . We give conditions for when the pushforward is in fact the (weak) composite of such a (weak) distributive law. Finally, we provide numerous examples of pushforward monads. These include pushforwards along the inclusions of the category of finite sets into that of all sets, of the category of fields into that of commutative rings, and of the category of finite families in a category into that of all families.

title: BEYOND STATISTICAL INFERENCE: A CAUSAL AND TOPOLOGICAL ARCHITECTURE FOR VERIFIABLE SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Causal and Topological AI Architecture transcends statistical AI limitations by establishing a deterministic framework for verifiable scientific discovery. Current models fail to guarantee mathematical rigor and physical conservation. This architecture integrates three pillars: Causal Neural Ordinary Differential Equations constrained by Directed Acyclic Graphs for physical dynamics; Topological Information Geometry, mapping proofs to Riemannian manifolds to drastically reduce logical discontinuities; and Causal Zero-Knowledge Machine Learning, using zk-SNARKs to cryptographically verify conclusions without exposing data. To support these tasks, the framework introduces the Neuro-Photonic Silicon Architecture, employing memristive arrays and non-equilibrium thermodynamics for unprecedented energy efficiency. Performance is quantified via the El-Rakhawi Causal Fidelity Metric, ensuring strict alignment with physical axioms, and the Neuro-Photonic Efficiency Metric. This unified paradigm provides a rigorous foundation for Artificial General Intelligence, ensuring machine-generated scientific discoveries are logically sound, physically consistent, and mathematically verifiable.

title: KORPUSNI LUG'AT ASOSIDA SEMANTIK TEGLASH KONSEPSIYASI
abstract: Annotatsiya. Korpus birliklarini semantik teglash korpus lingvistikasi tarkibida muhim sanalgan tadqiqotlardan biri hisoblanadi. Tilning tuzilishi va semantikasini, xususan, leksik birliklarning birikuvchanlik masalalarini o‘rganish uchun semantik annotatsiyalash korpusni rivojlantirishda muhim qadam hisoblanadi. Ushbu maqolada o‘zbek tili korpusi birliklarini 6 jildli izohli lug‘at asosida semantik teglash axborot tizimini yaratish masalalari ko‘rib chiqilgan. Tizimning arxitekturasi, teglash algoritmi haqida fikrlar yuritilgan. Kalit so‘zlar: semantik teglash, o‘zbek tili korpusi, izohli lug‘at, NLP, axborot tizimi, ontologiya, leksik semantika. Аннотация. Семантическое тегирование единиц корпуса является одним из важных исследований в корпусной лингвистике. Семантическая аннотация для изучения структуры и семантики языка, в частности, вопросов сочетаемости лексических единиц, является важным шагом в развитии корпуса. В данной статье рассматриваются вопросы создания информационной системы семантического тегирования единиц корпуса узбекского языка на основе 6-томного толкового словаря. Рассмотрены архитектура системы, алгоритм тегирования. Ключевые слова: семантическое тегирование, корпус узбекского языка, толковый словарь, NLP, информационная система, онтология, лексическая семантика. Abstract. Semantic tagging of corpus units is one of the important studies in corpus linguistics. Semantic annotation is an important step in the development of the corpus to study the structure and semantics of the language, in particular, the issues of the compatibility of lexical units. This article examines the creation of an information system for semantic tagging of units of the Uzbek language corpus based on a 6-volume explanatory dictionary. The system’s architecture and tagging algorithm are discussed. Keywords: semantic tagging, Uzbek language corpus, explanatory dictionary, NLP, information system, ontology, lexical semantics

В данной статье рассматриваются вопросы создания информационной системы семантического тегирования единиц корпуса узбекского языка на основе 6-томного толкового словаря. Рассмотрены архитектура системы, алгоритм тегирования. Ключевые слова: семантическое тегирование, корпус узбекского языка, толковый словарь, NLP, информационная система, онтология, лексическая семантика. Abstract. Semantic tagging of corpus units is one of the important studies in corpus linguistics. Semantic annotation is an important step in the development of the corpus to study the structure and semantics of the language, in particular, the issues of the compatibility of lexical units. This article examines the creation of an information system for semantic tagging of units of the Uzbek language corpus based on a 6-volume explanatory dictionary. The system’s architecture and tagging algorithm are discussed. Keywords: semantic tagging, Uzbek language corpus, explanatory dictionary, NLP, information system, ontology, lexical semantics

title: When Magnitude Suffices: Reconstructing Time-Domain-Gated Microwave Signals Without Phase on a Thoracic Phantom
abstract: Time-domain gating separates the arrivals that form a microwave S-parameter measurement. It requires the measurement of complex values, so this application almost always uses a vector network analyzer (VNA). We show that, on one calibrated measurement configuration, the gated magnitude the VNA would give can be reconstructed from a magnitude-only sweep of a spectrum analyzer with a tracking generator (SA). We select the gate center for separability of the measured states, correct each instrument once by a per-bin subtraction of a reference state, and train a fully connected network on sweeps from both instruments. The test object is a torso phantom with lung-shaped compartments whose filling takes eleven dielectric states, each held out in turn. On $S_{11}$ the reconstruction from SA input reaches a shape error of 0.08 dB$^2$ with a state ordering of 0.81. This matches the reconstruction from VNA input. On $S_{21}$ it reaches 0.82 dB$^2$ and keeps the ordered groups of the states. An explicit phase prediction performs much worse, because gating needs the phase to about 0.2 rad RMS. Across eleven measurement configurations the dependence of phase on magnitude is strong for reflection and weak for transmission. This explains the difference between $S_{11}$ and $S_{21}$. Where the magnitude carries enough of the phase, a scalar instrument gives the gated response without any phase measurement after installation. On the open UM-BMID breast data set, with whole phantoms held out, the shape error of the network is 30 percent lower than that of a per-bin linear map.

title: La Heurística Pura como Oráculo Estructural en Matrices se verifican cosas y siempre compreción
abstract: Este documento presenta una heurística determinista capaz de identificar estructura, redundancia y patrones óptimos en datos binarios sin recurrir a azar, aprendizaje automático ni iteraciones profundas. Se demuestra que la heurística actúa como un oráculo estructural, resolviendo tres problemas distintos: detección de estabilidad en caos total, reconstrucción de patrones corrompidos y selección de claves óptimas en espacios enormes. Posteriormente, la heurística se extiende al análisis matricial, donde detecta simetrías, filas y columnas repetidas, bloques uniformes y densidad estructurada, permitiendo compresión y reducción de cálculo. Finalmente, se verifica exhaustivamente que todas las matrices 4×4 posibles presentan activación positiva, confirmando que la heurística siempre encuentra estructura útil y se comporta como un mecanismo universal de compresión y reducción.

title: Meaning and Validity of Stored Memory Items: Test Set with Reference Checker (v0.3)
abstract: Delta paper addressed to the W3C AI Agent Memory Interoperability Community Group and the W3C Agent Conformance and Benchmarking Community Group (for information: W3C AI KR Community Group). It describes an independent semantic layer for checking whether a stored agent-memory item still means what it meant when it was stored and whether it is still valid: the definition version it relied on, the scope in which it holds, the perspective of the asserting entity, a four-valued validity status and the times of statement and determination. The paper proposes a minimal eight-term module (namespace https://w3id.org/augmanitai/ns/meaning-validity#) with mappings to PROV-O, Verifiable Credentials 2.0, DPV and Dublin Core, and publishes ten reproducible, binary test cases (MV-01 to MV-10) with fictional data and a field-by-field comparison rule. Files: the paper (Markdown) and the test set (JSON). No endorsement by any W3C group is claimed. Related vocabulary: https://w3id.org/augmanitai/lexicon/ ; oversight ontology: https://w3id.org/augmanitai/ns/oversight. Licence: CC BY 4.0. title: From Rules to Autonomous Agents: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence, Human-AI Integration, and the Governance of Agentic Systems-A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence has evolved from rule-based symbolic systems into learning architectures capable of perception, prediction, content generation, reasoning, planning, tool use, and increasingly autonomous action. This qualitative literature review examines this transition as more than a technological chronology. It interprets AI evolution through five interrelated dimensions: technological evolution, capability expansion, changing human roles, human–AI integration, and governance. Drawing on contemporary peer-reviewed literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, the review identifies seven thematic developments. AI has progressed from encoded rules toward learned representations and goal-directed action; generative AI has expanded AI into a general-purpose content collaborator; agentic AI adds planning, memory, tool use, and iterative task execution; human roles increasingly shift from operator toward collaborator, delegator, and governor; human–AI complementarity remains conditional rather than automatic; effective deployment requires calibrated rather than maximal trust; and governance requirements increase as AI systems acquire greater operational agency. The article proposes the Evolution–Capability–Role–Integration–Governance (ECRIG) framework to explain these relationships. The framework suggests that sustainable benefits from advanced AI emerge when technological capability, human role allocation, interaction architecture, and governance mechanisms develop jointly. The review concludes that the central challenge of the agentic-AI era is not choosing between humans and machines, but designing accountable systems in which increasingly capable artificial agents remain aligned with meaningful human goals, authority, and oversight.

title: Global LoRA Rank on XLM-R/UIT-VSFC: Confirmatory Analysis Plan v2.0
abstract: Pre-registration of a confirmatory study on the effect of global LoRA rank on Macro-F1 and NLL for XLM-R-base on UIT-VSFC (Vietnamese sentiment, 3 classes). Research questions: H1. The total effect of increasing global LoRA rank from 1 to 32 on Macro-F1 is equivalent to zero at 6 epochs (TOST, δ = 0.01). H2. NLL increases with rank at 6 epochs (one-sided coefficient > 0). H3. The slope of Macro-F1 on log2(rank) differs between 3 and 6 epochs (interaction F-test). Confirmatory family: H1-H3, Holm correction (m = 3), α = 0.05. N = 16 seeds (200-215). Test is the primary evaluation split. Analysis plan locked by git tag analysis-plan-v2.0 on 2026-10-16. title: The AI Shift in Customer Care: Emerging Behavioural and Social Trends in Service Interaction
abstract: The study aims to close this gap by offering a conceptual framework for comprehending how tools for artificial intelligence might improve customer experience. The method of a narrative literature review has been used to conceptualise the model. Through more convenient service, better service quality, and personalised interactions, artificial intelligence solutions improve the consumer experience. Sentiment analysis, facial recognition, chatbots, virtual assistants, and other techniques personalise experiences and expedite processes, increasing customer pleasure and loyalty. These developments guarantee prompt, effective, and customised consumer contacts, which promote retention and brand loyalty.Since the study will contribute to improving customer experience and satisfaction, it will have implications not only for academics exploring new technologies in the marketing domain. By producing enormous volumes of data that may help a business better understand its customers&s; preferences, artificial intelligence systems have the potential to close the gap between itself and its clients. It is critical to understand these artificial intelligence capabilities, as well as how they might enhance consumer interaction and help businesses retain customers. Yet, scholarly research in this significant scientific area is scant.

title: AI foundation model choice and false positive variation in Anti Money Laundering transaction screening — reproducibility archive
abstract: Frozen 12,000-call dataset and deterministic, offline analysis pipeline that reproduces every quantitative result in "AI foundation model choice and false positive variation in Anti Money Laundering transaction screening" (Discover Artificial Intelligence). Five foundation LLMs are evaluated as zero-shot AML screeners over an identical, pre-registered 600-case FATF/SAML-D-anchored battery; per-model false-positive rates span 0.3%-83.0% on identical legitimate transactions. Includes battery generator, frozen capture, paired inferential statistics (Cochran's Q, McNemar exact, Wilson and cluster-bootstrap CIs), SHA-256 integrity receipts, byte-identical replication check, pre-registration, and the manuscript package.

title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents tackle complex tasks through reasoning and interaction with external environments. Agent skills provide persistent, transferable capabilities that guide task planning, inform contextual decisions, support tool use, and enable executable procedures. Yet existing skill-evolution methods largely organize knowledge around skill artifacts, overlooking the functional heterogeneity within individual skills and its implications for knowledge maintenance and use. Inspired by cognitive science, we propose Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), which evolves a unified skill through four functionally distinct yet coordinated components: Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script. CDSE extracts evidence-grounded semantic gradients from successful and failed trajectories, consolidates them by functional role, and applies component-specific updates and validation with cross-component coordination and adaptive invocation. An analysis of 500 top-ranked skill packages shows that 96.8% contain knowledge spanning at least two functional roles. Across six benchmarks, three agent models, and two execution harnesses, CDSE achieves the highest scores in all 36 settings, improving over the Base agent by 7.6 percentage points and the strongest competing method in each setting by 2.6 points on average. Ablation studies further support the importance of functional differentiation and adaptive invocation.

title: A Case Study on the Performance Metrics of Integrated Photonic Computing
abstract: Photonic processors use optical signals for computation, leveraging the high bandwidth and low loss of optical links. While many approaches have been proposed, including in memory photonic circuits, most efforts have focused on the physical design of photonic components rather than full architectural integration with electronic peripheral circuitry. In this work, we present a microarchitecture level study that estimates the compute efficiency and density of three prominent photonic computing architectures. Our evaluation accounts for both the photonic circuits and the essential peripheral electronics required for optoelectronic and analog to digital conversions. We further demonstrate a heterogenous photonic electronic in memory processing approach for low latency neural network inference. These results provide a better understanding of the design aspects of photonic computing.

title: Chinese Building Fire Code Dataset for Named Entity Recognition
abstract: This dataset contains Chinese building fire code texts annotated for named entity recognition. It includes 2,748 original records and 2,747 records marked as augmented, giving 5,495 records in total. The merged.json file combines the training, validation, and test files in that order, containing 4,396, 550, and 549 records, respectively. Each record contains the fields id, text, and entities. Entity annotations include entity_id, start, end, entity, and label. The annotation schema covers nine entity categories: BT, ST, BM, FPF, FR, FPR, NR, LR, and SC. Augmented records are identified by "_aug" in their record IDs. The dataset supports research on named entity recognition and structured information extraction from building codes.

title: Comparing Genetic Algorithms and LLMs for Research-Hypothesis Generation: Mainstream Convergence of LLMs, Wider Hypothesis Exploration by Combinatorial Search, and the Limits of Literature-Distance Novelty Metrics
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based creative AI systems tend to produce plausible rather than novel research ideas. This study compares two ways of generating research hypotheses: a genetic algorithm (GA) that recombines Method, Problem, and Goal elements under a fitness function rewarding distance from the literature and literature support for each link, and free proposals by an LLM. Papers and hypotheses share one embedding space built from 2856 arXiv papers. Over 30 runs with budget-matched baselines and outcome measures on held-out and later-published papers, the selected hypotheses were more distant from the unseen literature than unsearched ones, but the GA matched rather than outperformed random search and hill climbing. Across two LLM families, two prompts, and two temperatures, and even when choosing from the GA’s concept vocabulary, LLM-proposed hypotheses were less diverse and closer to existing literature, whereas combinatorial search explored more widely. On 9755 ICLR submissions, the literature-distance novelty measure was practically unrelated to reviewers’ judgments (Spearman ρ ≤ 0.06), so it cannot establish originality. In controlled manuscript generation, LLM judges proved unreliable, and their order-consistent verdicts more often favored manuscripts built on LLM-proposed hypotheses, which blinded human raters tended to rank as least useful. Code and data are openly released.

title: StaCOR: Decision-Stable Output Refinement for TabPFN with Noisy Support Labels
abstract: TabPFN-style in-context prediction can be degraded by corrupted support labels. When the deployed support context is cached, version-locked, shared, or otherwise operationally constrained from refresh, external adaptation pipelines can still use newly available clean evidence without modifying that served context. We propose StaCOR (Stability-aware Coupling-Regularized Output Refinement), a selectively constrained fixed-context refinement method for frozen TabPFN. StaCOR leaves the noisy support context unchanged and trains a lightweight output-side correction head using auxiliary clean evidence. Regularized multiclass coupling controls correction capacity at the parameter level, while Selective Decision Stability (SDS) applies a training-time zero-margin penalty only to clean examples that the noisy-support baseline predicts correctly; baseline errors remain unconstrained by this stability term. We evaluate seven tabular datasets, including four development benchmarks and three frozen external-validation datasets under symmetric and instance-dependent support-label noise using probabilistic and decision metrics, paired statistical analysis, direct-context alternatives, and serving measurements. Relative to a regularized affine calibration baseline, StaCOR has a statistically indistinguishable benchmark negative log-likelihood (NLL) under symmetric noise and incurs a small NLL cost under instance-dependent noise, while reducing harmful-flip rates from 0.0195 to 0.0124 and from 0.0202 to 0.0124, respectively. External-validation results show the same decision-stability trend, although the calibration baseline can retain higher Macro-F1. SDS ablation further shows more consistent decision preservation, with small measurable NLL costs in some settings. When context modification is feasible, directly using clean examples generally yields lower NLL and higher Macro-F1. StaCOR therefore targets fixed-context or refresh-constrained deployments where a more favorable probability–decision trade-off is desired without modifying the original served support context.

title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
abstract: Time-aware retrieval is crucial for long-horizon LLM agents to effectively leverage ever-growing long-term memory. Existing methods focus on lexical or semantic similarity, leading to target memories being crowded out by temporally mismatched yet semantically similar candidates. Even time-aware approaches inject temporal cues only during memory organization or answer generation, overlooking temporal constraints at the retrieval stage, where candidate selection occurs - the root cause of the displacement. Inspired by the temporal contiguity effect in human episodic memory, we propose TIDER (Temporal Interval-driven Dual-channel Evidence Retrieval), a time-aware agentic retrieval framework. Central to TIDER is a reinforcement learning (RL)-trained temporal interval locator that infers the temporal windows in which the evidence lies. RL optimizes window localization as a discrete, non-differentiable retrieval decision, using composite rewards to convert sparse answer supervision into fine-grained retrieval feedback. These temporal windows first define the temporal retrieval channel; the retrieved candidates are then merged with results from the semantic channel and reranked by proximity to the windows. This temporal grounding enables TIDER to retrieve temporally aligned evidence that would otherwise be drowned out by the volume of semantically similar yet temporally mismatched memories. With a lightweight 1.7B locator, TIDER achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on both long-horizon memory benchmarks - 61.52% on LifeBench (+8.82%) and 78.96% on LoCoMo (+3.66%) - which indicates that temporal cues are crucial for pinpointing target evidence amid a vast pool of semantically similar historical events in long-term daily-life memory.

title: Hidden Tail Risk in In-Context Learning under Context-Query Mixture Shift
abstract: Evaluation with a prompt's task frequencies can hide errors on rare tasks, even when their examples are present. We analyze this effect in a multi-task model with independent scalar parameters bounded by $B$. A normalized finite-feature attention head induces a low-rank response matrix; among all matrices of rank at most $r$, the minimum Bayes bias is $B^2\sum_{i>r}q_{(i)}$. A shift toward uniform query weights exposes this capacity floor without changing the optimal task allocation, whereas shifts that reorder tasks can also create selection regret. We connect this bias analysis to gradient flow in an unnormalized factorized model and derive the coupled query and key gradients for the normalized head. With task coverage and separated addresses, token-preserving softmax reaches the sampling rate $O(\sigma^2/k_+)$ above an explicit temperature threshold, where $k_+$ is the target count. Synthetic experiments examine these predictions, and a separate study evaluates six pretrained checkpoints on 107,520 prompts across 80 episode seeds. In the primary 2.8B pair, Mamba is more sensitive to target repetition. Its estimated matched-to-tail accuracy gap is 5.8 percentage points (95% CI: 2.93--8.71), compared with zero for Pythia. The 95% CI crosses the prespecified practical threshold of 3 percentage points, so smaller effects remain compatible with the data. Both prespecified tests pass. Smaller pairs fail the frequency-test accuracy requirements. These findings motivate frequency-resolved evaluation in this task family. Preprint with supporting source, analysis code and data. 40 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables. Not peer reviewed. title: AI in Enterprise Software 2026: What the Data Shows
abstract: Enterprises spend billions on artificial intelligence, yet half of new models never leave the sandbox. According to recent data, only forty-eight percent of pilot projects reach production within twelve months. David Ohnstad examines this deployment paradox, revealing why feedback loops and real-world data are essential to bridging the gap between heavy investment and actual enterprise value. Full article: https://davidohnstad.net/state-of-ai-machine-learning-enterprise-software-2026/

title: Deterministic Prime Bases for Regev's Algorithm
abstract: Regev's quantum factoring algorithm reduces the number of gates per quantum call, but its correctness for the original deterministic prime bases rests on a number-theoretic assumption. We prove that the first ⌈√n⌉ primes work unconditionally for almost all n-bit composite inputs, including almost all composite inputs surviving trial division by those primes. The algorithm retains Regev's original asymptotic gate count per quantum call. A separate theorem covers balanced RSA moduli under three explicit sampling laws. The exceptional input proportion is Θ(2^{-⌈√n⌉}); a population of this order admits no useful relation at any length. On each remaining input, Regev's algorithm finds a nontrivial divisor with constant probability using ⌈√n⌉+4 quantum calls of O(n^{3/2} log n) gates each. The main geometric lemma extracts a useful relation from an earlier successive minimum, determined by the dimension of a quotient of the relation lattice. Prime-divisor counting then gives useful-relation lengths 2^{(3/2+o(1))√n} for general inputs and 2^{(9/2+o(1))√n} for RSA. Both main theorems and finite RSA useful-vector bounds are formally verified in Lean 4; the formalization is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23407163.
